cards.text: Meet Hosea, a prophet the word of the LORD came to (Hosea 1:1). In the last chapter of his book, he calls out, "Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God…" Friend, that's a door being held WIDE open.

cards.question: Hosea tells Israel why they need to come back to the LORD. What does he say happened to them?

answers.text: They lost their way in the desert

cards.text: And Hosea doesn't just say come home. He tells them what to bring AND what to say, like a friend who writes your whole apology text and then hands you back the phone.

cards.question: Israel has stumbled by their iniquity. Hosea tells them to bring their ___ and return to the LORD.

cards.text: Then come the words. Hosea gives Israel exactly what to say to the LORD, and it starts with their iniquity.

cards.question: In the words Hosea gives Israel, how much of their iniquity do they ask the LORD to take away?

cards.text: ALL of it. No "just the little stuff, Lord, I'll handle the rest." They ask Him to receive them graciously, so they can present the fruit of their lips.

Next, they name what they won't count on anymore: "Assyria will not save us, nor will we ride on horses." It's like finally deleting the number of the guy who keeps promising he'll pay you back on Friday.

cards.question: Israel says Assyria will not save them. In the words Hosea gives them, who are they turning to instead?

cards.text: Then comes the big one, and I bet this one was the hardest to say out loud.

cards.question: In the words Hosea gives Israel, they promise never again to call the work of their own hands their gods.
With every other helper given up, Israel ends with why they're turning to the LORD: in Him the ___ find compassion.

cards.text: Those are the words Hosea gives Israel to bring back. Now the LORD speaks, and I'm leaning in like a guy who just sent that apology text and is staring at the little typing dots.

cards.question: The LORD speaks about Israel's apostasy. What does He say He'll do with it?
The LORD says He will love Israel only after they earn it.
The LORD says He will freely love Israel, because His ___ has turned away from them.

cards.text: Then the LORD's message turns into a GARDEN. And first, He picks a picture for what He'll be to Israel.

cards.question: In the LORD's garden picture, He says He will be like the ___ to Israel.
In the LORD's garden picture, Israel will wither like grass in the sun.

cards.text: Instead, Israel will blossom like the lily and take root like the cedars of Lebanon. Flowers on top AND roots underneath, friend.

Israel's splendor will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon. Friend, after years in a junk drawer I smelled like dust and old receipts, and Israel's about to smell like CEDAR.
Then the LORD says, "They will return and dwell in his shade…" Israel's not the little plant looking for shade anymore. Israel IS the shade.

cards.question: In the LORD's garden picture, they will dwell in Israel's shade and grow ___.

cards.text: They'll blossom like the vine, too. And Israel's renown will be like the wine of Lebanon, friend. That's FAMOUS.
Then the LORD calls out to Ephraim, another name Hosea uses for Israel (Hosea 11:8): "O Ephraim, what have I to do anymore with idols?" That's a question with the answer baked right in.

cards.question: With the idols out of the picture, the LORD says it is He who answers Ephraim and watches over him.

cards.text: Then the LORD puts Himself right into the garden picture: "I am like a flourishing cypress…"

cards.question: The LORD says He is like a flourishing cypress. Where does He tell Ephraim his fruit comes from?

cards.text: Hosea closes with a word for anyone listening: whoever is wise, let him understand these things. The ways of the LORD are right.

cards.question: Hosea says the ways of the LORD are right. What happens to the rebellious in those ways?

findings.problem: The right answer, "They stumbled by their iniquity," is the only answer in Bible wording ('stumbled', 'iniquity'). The two wrong answers are plain modern phrasing, so the right one stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: "ALL of it.", the made-up line, and "They ask Him to receive them graciously...". It also says Israel asks. In the text, Hosea only tells them what to say ("Say to Him: ...", 14:2). Israel never says it in the passage.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "They ask Him to receive them graciously" calls Hosea's instruction something Israel did. The text gives these as words Israel is told to say (14:2). Cards 9 and 11 word it correctly as "the words Hosea gives" them.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Next, they name what they won't count on anymore" says Israel speaks these words. In 14:2-3 they are words Hosea tells Israel to say.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Israel ends with why they're turning to the LORD" presents Israel as the speaker. The line is part of the words Hosea gives Israel to say (14:2-3).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Card 1 already quotes "Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God", and cards 3 and 5 say the words are spoken to the LORD. That gives away the answer "The LORD their God" before the question is asked.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card tells nothing from the passage. It only teases the next question ("Then comes the big one...").

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: the quote line, "Israel's not the little plant looking for shade anymore." and "Israel IS the shade."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: "They'll blossom like the vine, too.", "And Israel's renown will be like the wine of Lebanon, friend." and "That's FAMOUS."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "A word for anyone listening" widens who is addressed. The text speaks to "whoever is wise" and "whoever is discerning" (14:9). The card also names Hosea as the speaker of the closing verse, which the text doesn't do.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never tells "the righteous walk in them" (14:9). The passage's last line contrasts the righteous with the rebellious, and only the rebellious half is covered.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "They get lost in them" is close in meaning to the right answer "They stumble in them". Both describe failing to walk the LORD's ways, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
